text: And 'tis also folly and injustice to deprive children, when grown up, of familiarity with their father, and to carry a scornful and austere countenance toward them, thinking by that to keep them in awe and obedience; for it is a very idle farce that, instead of producing the effect designed, renders fathers distasteful, and, which is worse, ridiculous to their own children.
author: Michel de Montaigne
locator: Book II, Chapter 8, Of the Affection of Fathers to their Children
translation: Charles Cotton, ed. W. C. Hazlitt, 1877
